correctness.rationale: The characteristic-two Rota–Baxter equation at x=y yields R(x)^2=0; independence of natural-basis squares forces every R(x) into the annihilator <e_n>. Conversely all annihilator-valued linear maps satisfy the equation. Each algebra automorphism must send e1 to a e1+b en, a nonzero, since successive squares and mixed-product orthogonality kill other coefficients; hence phi_{a,b}(ei)=a^{2^{i-1}}ei for i>=2, group order q(q-1). Comparing R′phi=phi R gives c′_n=c_n, c′_i=a^{2^{n-1}-2^{i-1}}c_i (2<=i<n), c′_1=a^{2^{n-1}-1}c_1-(b/a)c_n. When c_n=0 the free b-stabilizer adds factor q, and a-stabilizer order is gcd(q-1,{2^{n-i}-1})=h(J). When c_n≠0, b is uniquely fixed by a and each orbit acquires q factor. Counting coefficient vectors by support gives t^{|J|-1}h(J) orbits for every nonempty J. Burnside on the cyclic F_q^× gives the divisor formula. Independently enumerated binary extension field conjugation orbits at (q,n)=(2,2),(2,4),(4,2),(4,3),(4,4),(8,3),(8,4); counts 3,12,5,14,48,24,150 and predicted stabilizer/orbit sizes matched. Symbolic proof applies to every n,e, small cases are not extrapolated.

final_claim: For a pure nilpotent evolution chain E_n over F_{2^e}, all weight-zero Rota–Baxter operators map into the last basis line. Under the full automorphism group of size q(q-1), the terminal coefficient c_n is invariant; support sets J have stabilizer sizes given by h(J)=2^gcd(e,{n-i:i in J})-1, with exact orbit-size/count formulas and Burnside divisor sum O_n(q)=1/(q-1) sum_{d|q-1} phi(d)[q^floor((n-1)/ord_d(2))+(q-1)q^floor((n-2)/ord_d(2))].
